newsitem.title: UK: Airfreight industry can save $2bln a year - forwarder.
newsitem.headline: Airfreight industry can save $2bln a year - forwarder.

text.p: The removal of global duplication could save the airfreight industry more than $2 billion annually, said Jean Godart, executive vice-president airfreight at Swiss forwarders Kuehne & Nagel AG.
He told an airfreight conference here, such a saving equals about 10 percent of the industry's worldwide turnover, or triple its profits.
Productivity would be increased drastically by shippers, forwarders, airlines and consignees jointly focusing on what does not need to be done and thus eliminating unnecessary processes.
For example, Godart asked why airlines applied different tariffs from every individual country in Europe to intercontinental or intra-European destinations.

"Would it not make sense to elaborate on simple, European-wide common-rated and transparent rate packages in line with economic facts -- to clearly defined traffic areas worldwide -- instead of complicating matters through an untransparent rate jungle?" he said.
The only issue which mattered was the clear definition of costs and the add-on of an appropriate profit margin.
Godart also questioned why rates were not published in one currency, for example the Euro or the U.S. dollar, which he said would allow an easy and transparent rate comparison worldwide.
This would give the airfreight industry a global character instead of sticking to "old-fashioned natonal egotistic and monopolistic policies and hiding behind today's tariff inefficiencies".
Godart said it would make sense to increase service quality for shippers "through redefining new structural concepts forwarders and airlines offer".

Daily air cargo uplift possibilities should be used instead of freight being consolidated up to weekends, which resulted in trucking goods at high cost throughout Europe and also creating artificial backlogs and tremendous costs at airports worldwide.
Godart urged that forwarder/airline research and development units be set up to resolve common problems.

He estimated the global freight forwarding industry at best makes a profit of $800 million annually, or two percent of its revenue. If airlines performed at the same level, he projected a best case airline/forwarder global combined profit of $1.2 billion a year, way below many other industries.

Godart said the airfreight industry was unique in lacking any joint capacity and route planning between airlines and their major distribution channel, the forwarders, which buy more than 90 percent of the available capacity. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
